Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important chase! The umpires and the players are back out in the middle and it will be the duo of Tammy Beaumont and Maia Bouchier to open the innings for England Women. Megan Schutt to start proceedings with the new ball. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, 309 is a big number to get and for a team that has struggled to score in excess of 200 runs so far in the series, it becomes even more difficult. England Women's highest successful chase against Australia Women stands at 264 but their highest successful chase in Australia stands at just 213 runs. With everything stacked against them, can England Women turn things around with a big batting display? We shall find out. Join us in a few minutes' time for the second essay.

With 300 still on the cards, the Aussies did falter a touch and Natalie Sciver-Brunt was able to get rid of both set batters, allowing the visitors to curtail the damage to an extent. However, that wasn't the case as Georgia Wareham, playing her first game of the series, came in and smashed an unbeaten 38 off just 12 balls, taking the number one spinner in the world, Sophie Ecclestone apart at the death as well.

England Women had the opportunity to tighten the screws but instead, the Aussies attacked them more as Gardner built another big partnership, this time with Tahlia McGrath and it was a quick one as well. Gardner went on to notch up a maiden ODI ton as McGrath brought up her half-century in quick time and the pair put on 103 runs for the 6th wicket partnership.

However, the pitch did ease out and batting became a lot easier but still a big partnership was needed and Australia got just that through the pair of Beth Mooney and Ash Gardner who put on 95 runs before Mooney got to fifty and out giving Charlie Dean her second wicket.

Australia Women were a bit shaky to begin with and Phoebe Litchfield fell quite early before the likes of Ellyse Perry and Alyssa Healy soon followed suit and they lost 3 wickets in the Powerplay. This soon became 59 for 4 as Annabel Sutherland fell too. The English bowlers were riding high at this stage and their pacers had set up the game brilliantly.

That is some batting display from the Aussies! And what seemed to be heading towards a third straight low-scoring affair has turned out to be a big first innings score thanks to some insane hitting in the final 10 overs.

England Women on the other hand simply haven't batted to their potential and for all their stellar efforts with the ball, they haven't got anything to show for it so far. Hello and a very warm welcome to our coverage of the Women's Ashes. Two of women's cricket's finest teams reignite an age old rivalry in this multi format series and it is now time for the 3rd ODI set to be played at the Bellerive Oval in Hobart.
... MATCH DAY ...

One of cricket’s fiercest rivalries takes center stage, but this time it’s the Women’s turn to feel the heat! Australia Women have already wrapped up the ODI series, but the hosts will be hungry to deliver a whitewash at the iconic Ninja Stadium in Bellerive. The Aussies are riding high after a nail-biting win in the second game, defending a modest total of 180. Spin has been the story of the series so far, with Alana King dazzling in superb form, claiming six wickets in two games. Ash Gardner’s versatility adds more depth - not only is she a crucial part of the spin arsenal, but her batting prowess in the middle order provides stability. Skipper Alyssa Healy set the tone with a classy half-century in the opening game, while Ellyse Perry’s gritty knock was instrumental in giving Australia a fighting chance last time. The likes of Phoebe Litchfield, Beth Mooney, and Tahlia McGrath will look to make a bigger impact, while Annabel Sutherland’s all-round brilliance makes her a player to watch. The pace trio of Megan Schutt, Kim Garth, and Darcie Brown have been relentless, and their familiarity with home conditions gives Australia an undeniable edge. For England Women, the series has been a tale of missed opportunities. Heather Knight’s side has struggled to fire with the bat, leaving their bowling efforts unsupported. Maia Bouchier and Tammy Beaumont must rise to the occasion and provide solid starts, while experienced campaigners like Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Natalie Sciver-Brunt hold the key to their middle-order fightback. Amy Jones was the lone warrior in the last game, almost snatching victory, but lacked support at the other end. On the bowling front, Sophie Ecclestone has lived up to her reputation as the No. 1 bowler in the world, while Alice Capsey and Charlie Dean have done well to back her up. Lauren Bell and Lauren Filer lead the pace attack admirably, but they need runs to defend. Can England Women finally break through and grab their first win of the series, or will the Aussies finish with a clean sweep? Stay tuned - it’s all to play for!
